---
title: Study specs
guide-section: "Reproducible requests"
---

A study spec describes a study request in a JSON or YAML file: the archetype, the seed, the number
of subjects, the controls, any defects, and the outputs. It is the same request as a `tf.study()`
call, in a form you can keep under version control, share, and run from Python, R or the command
line. The format is defined by a [JSON Schema](https://github.com/rich-iannone/trialforge/blob/main/spec/study-spec.schema.json).

A spec is useful when the request matters more than the code around it: a reference study a team
tests against, the input of a CI job, or a study you want to hand to someone who uses R or the
command line instead of Python.

## A spec

This one asks for a 12-week hypertension study with 240 subjects, written as a submission package:

```yaml
spec_version: 0                       # the spec format version; 0 is the only one so far
study:
  archetype: parallel_continuous      # the study type (see tf.archetypes())
  studyid: HTN001                     # STUDYID; each archetype has a default
  seed: 20261013                      # required: a spec always describes one exact study
  standards: { sdtmig: "3.4", adamig: "1.3", define: "2.1" }
population:
  n: 240                              # randomized subjects (300 if omitted)
controls:                             # merged over the archetype's defaults
  indication: hypertension
  weeks: 12
  change: [-4, -11]                   # mean change at week 12: placebo, Drug A (mmHg)
  dropout_rate: 0.12
outputs:
  layout: submission                  # sdtm/ and adam/ with XPT and define.xml
```

The sections:

- `study`{.gd-no-link}: the archetype, the seed and optionally `studyid`{.gd-no-link}. The seed is
required, unlike in `tf.study()`, because a spec without one wouldn't describe a single study.
`standards`, when given, must name the versions this build supports: SDTMIG 3.4, ADaMIG 1.3,
Define-XML 2.1 and the 2024-09-27 CDISC controlled terminology (`ct`). Stating them makes the spec
fail loudly, rather than silently give different data, if it is run by a build with other versions.
- `population`: `n`, the number of randomized subjects (300 if omitted).
- `controls`{.gd-no-link}: the archetype's controls, merged over its defaults (see
[Archetypes and controls](03-archetypes.qmd)). They are checked exactly as `tf.study()` checks
keyword arguments.
- `data_quality`: `defects`{.gd-no-link}, a profile name or a mapping of defect types to counts
and rates (see [Seeded defects](07-defects.qmd)).
- `outputs`: for the command-line tool, the `layout` (`submission` or `flat`, the default) and, for
`flat`, the `formats`{.gd-no-link} (`[xpt]` by default).

The schema also sketches sections for later releases (`design`, `endpoints`, `safety`, `dropout`).
A spec that uses them is an error rather than being silently ignored.

## From Python

`tf.study_from_spec()` takes a path to a JSON or YAML file, the text itself, or a dict:

```{python}
import trialforge as tf

spec = """
study:
  archetype: parallel_continuous
  seed: 1
population:
  n: 300
controls:
  indication: hypertension
  weeks: 12
"""
from_spec = tf.study_from_spec(spec)
from_spec
```

It is the same study as the equivalent `tf.study()` call:

```{python}
direct = tf.study("parallel_continuous", n=300, seed=1, indication="hypertension", weeks=12)
from_spec.define_xml("adam") == direct.define_xml("adam") and from_spec.truth == direct.truth
```

A dict works the same way, which is handy when the spec is built in code:

```{python}
tf.study_from_spec(
    {
        "study": {"archetype": "vaccine", "seed": 7},
        "population": {"n": 50},
        "controls": {"doses": 1},
        "data_quality": {"defects": "light"},
    }
)
```

`study_from_spec()` takes the same `output` argument as `tf.study()`. The `outputs` section is for
the command-line tool; from Python, write files with `Study.write()` or `Study.write_submission()`.

## Errors

A spec is checked in full before anything is generated, and every part of it is checked strictly: a
misspelled key is an error, never ignored. A spec without a seed:

```{python}
try:
    tf.study_from_spec("study:\n  archetype: parallel_continuous\n")
except ValueError as e:
    print(e)
```

A misspelled section:

```{python}
try:
    tf.study_from_spec(
        "study:\n  archetype: parallel_continuous\n  seed: 1\npopulaton:\n  n: 100\n"
    )
except ValueError as e:
    print(e)
```

A section reserved for a later release:

```{python}
try:
    tf.study_from_spec(
        "study:\n  archetype: parallel_continuous\n  seed: 1\ndropout:\n  rate: 0.1\n"
    )
except ValueError as e:
    print(e)
```

A standard this build doesn't support:

```{python}
try:
    tf.study_from_spec(
        "study:\n  archetype: parallel_continuous\n  seed: 1\n  standards: {sdtmig: '3.3'}\n"
    )
except ValueError as e:
    print(e)
```

Misspelled controls and defect types give the same errors as in `tf.study()`.

## Saving a request as a spec

A study records everything a spec needs, so you can turn a study made in code into a spec file.
`Study.controls` holds every control, defaults included:

```{python}
import json

trial = tf.study("parallel_continuous", n=200, seed=5, indication="obesity", weeks=52)
saved = {
    "spec_version": 0,
    "study": {"archetype": trial.archetype, "studyid": trial.studyid, "seed": trial.seed},
    "population": {"n": trial.truth["n"]},
    "controls": trial.controls,
}
print(json.dumps(saved, indent=2))
```

A `null` control takes its value from another one: here `change`{.gd-no-link} comes from the
indication's preset, and there is no non-inferiority margin. Add a `data_quality` section by hand if
the study had defects. Regenerating from the spec gives the same study:

```{python}
tf.study_from_spec(saved).truth == trial.truth
```

## From the command line

The `trialforge` command-line tool generates a study from a spec and writes it as the spec's
`outputs` section asks:

```bash
trialforge generate examples/hypertension.yaml -o out/
trialforge summary examples/hypertension.yaml   # datasets and truth manifest, nothing written
trialforge archetypes
trialforge controls parallel_continuous
```

`generate` writes to `trialforge-out/` unless `-o` names another directory. `--formats xpt,csv`
overrides the spec's formats (and its layout), and `--submission` writes the submission layout
whatever the spec says. `summary` prints each dataset's row count, the verification result, any
defects and the truth manifest, so it is a quick way to see what a spec gives.

The command-line tool is a Rust program, separate from the Python package. Install it with Cargo
(from [rustup](https://rustup.rs)):

```bash
cargo install --git https://github.com/rich-iannone/trialforge trialforge-cli
```

or, from a clone of the repository, `cargo install --path crates/trialforge-cli`. It writes every
format, Parquet included, and gives the same data as the Python and R packages of the same version.
